clue.text: Grave in Lemnos turned over

indicators.note: turned over tells us to churn up the island's name Lemnos and lay its letters out afresh

explanation.surface: Something solemn and serious is found on a Greek island that has been overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' looks like a reversal, but Lemnos backwards is SONMEL; it signals a rearrangement of LEMNOS instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and solemn are synonyms, both describing a serious, dignified manner.

clue.text: Flat lock is a frontal feature

definitions.text: Flat lock is a frontal feature

parts.words: Flat lock is a frontal feature
parts.note: a flat lock of hair pressed onto the forehead, a hairstyle feature at the front of the head; 'flat lock' suggests a door fitting

explanation.surface: A remark about a flat lock fitted to the front of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss curl is a small curl of hair lying flat on the forehead or cheek.

clue.text: Earthbound? Absolutely

definitions.meaning: heading all the way to the earth, with a question mark because this is the literal reading of the idiom
completely, utterly, as in 'that suits me'

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, falling right to the soil; as an idiom, the phrase means completely or perfectly.

clue.text: Power to live and be at the head

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: A ruler needs strength, a home, and a place at the top table.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair or take charge of a meeting, sitting at its head.

clue.text: Smashing botanist perhaps and believer in the miraculous

parts.note: smashing, as British slang for excellent, means super
a botanist is one kind of naturalist, someone who studies nature

explanation.surface: A brilliant plant scientist who also believes in miracles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' is British slang for excellent, so SUPER, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernaturalist holds that there are forces beyond nature, such as miracles.

clue.text: Rag doll worth, to me, about twopence

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Rag doll worth, to me, about twopence': MO(PP)ET needs MOET from 'to me', but no word signals rearranging it ('worth' looks like an OCR garble of the anagram indicator), so the parse cannot be completed honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Rag doll worth, to me, about twopence

clue.text: Shock seeing bats in reverse order

indicators.note: in reverse order asks for the synonym of bats to be written from its end to its start

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to see a flock of bats flying backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' is not the animal but slang for mad, giving NUTS, which runs backwards to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock and to stun both mean to stupefy or astonish someone.

clue.text: Gravity attaching to witchcraft in desert

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravity or its acceleration in physics
obi (or obeah) is a form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Gravity and magic combine somewhere in a barren wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: OBI, the West Indian folk magic also spelt obeah, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Inboard propeller

parts.note: an inboard propeller sounds like a boat's engine part, but the device used to drive a rowing boat is pulled from inside the boat

explanation.surface: A technical note about the screw of a motor launch.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar propels a rowing boat, worked by a rower sitting inside the hull.

clue.text: The low tars in them dam damaged our ratings …

definitions.text: The low tars in them dam damaged our ratings

parts.words: The low tars in them dam damaged our ratings
parts.note: the 'low' sailors are those who travel beneath the waves, and their craft harmed the British seamen (ratings) in wartime

explanation.surface: A gloomy line about sailors sinking in the estimation of a navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary naval seamen; 'low' means underwater, so the vessels are German submarines of the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines that sank Allied ships and drowned their crews.

clue.text: Hold the high tar

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip applied from behind with arms under the opponent's
the admiral standing on a tall column in Trafalgar Square, London: a sailor (tar) set high up

explanation.definitionFit: A full or half nelson is a wrestling grip; Admiral Nelson's statue tops a column in London.

clue.text: Well off, perhaps, in retirement

parts.note: 'off' can mean asleep and 'retirement' going to bed, so this is someone soundly dozing once they have gone to bed, not a rich pensioner

explanation.surface: A comment that pensioners may be comfortably wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleeping has dropped off, well away, having retired for the night.

clue.text: Do Britain's union characters develop such defiance of authority?

indicators.note: the characters, that is the letters, of the three words develop into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A question whether British trade unions encourage people to disobey their bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters develop' rearranges the letters of DO BRITAINS UNION, the apostrophe ignored but the S kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Insubordination is refusal to obey those in charge, which is defiance of authority.

clue.text: Expression of triumphant surprise when I leave Midwestern state

indicators.note: when I leave says the letter I is to go out of the state's name

parts.note: Ohio is a state in the American Midwest

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims with glee on finally getting out of the Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oho is an exclamation of surprise or triumph, as when catching someone out.

clue.text: Breaking the law, you# begin to be comfortably off

indicators.note: breaking means the words the law are smashed and put back together differently
you begin points to the opening letter of you

explanation.surface: Advice that crime is the way to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges THE LAW into WEALTH; 'you begin' adds the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy means rich, and comfortably off is a gentler way of saying the same.

clue.text: Letter from Greece airline relies on, in short

definitions.meaning: the seventh character of the Greek alphabet
the abbreviation for estimated time of arrival, which airlines depend on

explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a Greek alphabet character; ETA abbreviates estimated time of arrival, vital to airline schedules.

clue.text: Cheese made unnaturally high?

parts.note: split the cheese's name to get the answer: something raised artificially by having stilts on

explanation.surface: A complaint about cheese that smells too strong or has been overpriced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' cheese suggests strong or ripe smell, but the reading is a cheese name broken as STILT-ON, raised on stilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a crumbly blue English cheese.

clue.text: Pop article in French newspaper

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the paper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece about pop music in a Paris paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests music, but it is the fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is an informal word for a fizzy soft drink such as lemonade.

clue.text: Stuff during tea-break

parts.note: over means during, as in 'over the holidays'

indicators.note: break tells us to split up the word tea and reorder its letters

explanation.surface: Something gets stuffed during a tea-break at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea-break' reads as one word, but 'break' rearranges TEA to EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to gorge, eating far too much.

clue.text: Do rule in the house

parts.note: 'do' is a celebration or social event and 'rule' is governance, while 'the house' is the parliament where political groups hold power

explanation.surface: An instruction to obey the domestic rules at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do rule' reads as an order to follow house rules; read as nouns, a do is a party and rule is government.
explanation.definitionFit: Party government is the system where the largest political group in parliament forms the administration.

clue.text: Subject for doctorate he sits, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of he sits might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A doctoral candidate sitting down to work on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctoral thesis is the long dissertation on a topic submitted for a PhD.

clue.text: French port St Anne converted

indicators.note: converted means the letters of St Anne are changed into a different order

explanation.surface: A saint converted in a French harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suggests religion beside St Anne, but it rearranges her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a port city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Players' entrance at Wembley?

parts.note: a team is a side, so a way in for a football team at the national stadium becomes a team's door

explanation.surface: Asking where footballers walk out at Wembley, England's national stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is England's national football stadium in London; a team is a 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: A side door is a secondary entrance at the side of a building.

clue.text: To edge forward a little at a time is socially acceptable at church

definitions.text: To edge forward a little at a time

parts.note: in means fashionable or socially acceptable, as in 'the in crowd'

explanation.surface: Creeping forward slowly is considered proper behaviour in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch along is to creep forward by tiny degrees.

clue.text: The Ag in cloudage?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, recalling the saying that every cloud has a silver edge on its inside

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle about silver in an age of cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Ag is silver; the proverb 'every cloud has a silver lining' supplies the word after silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver lining is the bright side of a cloud in the proverb, so the silver is its inner layer.

clue.text: Fighting a lawsuit .

definitions.meaning: combat, as in soldiers seeing combat
a legal case brought in court

explanation.definitionFit: Troops 'in action' are in combat; an action is also a civil case brought in court.

clue.text: Foolish sort helping Euclid to build a bridge

definitions.text: helping Euclid to build a bridge
definitions.meaning: Euclid's fifth proposition is called the pons asinorum, Latin for the bridge of donkeys, since dull pupils stumbled over it

explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is called a donkey, and Euclid's theorem on isosceles triangles is the 'bridge of donkeys'.

clue.text: Parliament to keep fasting

definitions.meaning: a legislative assembly, as in Japan's or the historic Holy Roman Empire's
to restrict one's eating, keeping to a regime of little food

explanation.definitionFit: Japan's legislature is the Diet; to diet is to limit one's food intake.
